claims.text: The two groups show distinct error signatures that can be directly linked to the hardware components they report on; in Group R30‑M0‑N9‑C:J16‑U01 every line records a **KERNEL FATAL data TLB error interrupt**, indicating repeated fatal failures of the Translation Lookaside Buffer for data accesses, while Group R02‑M1‑N0‑C:J12‑U11 contains only **KERNEL INFO instruction cache parity error corrected** messages that note non‑fatal parity problems in the instruction cache and are logged far less frequently.

The fatal TLB errors appear in a tight, continuous burst spanning from 17:32 to 23:26 on June 11 2005 with timestamps only seconds apart, suggesting an ongoing hardware fault that is not being cleared by software, whereas the instruction‑cache parity events are spaced days apart and never escalate to a fatal condition.

Because the R30 node exhibits a sustained pattern of fatal TLB interrupts without any intervening corrective messages, its behavior is more anomalous and points to a deeper memory‑coherency or processor‑internal fault.

The root‑cause hypothesis is that a defective data‑TLB entry or a hardware defect in the TLB replacement logic on R30‑M0‑N9‑C:J16‑U01 is causing repeated fatal errors, leading to system instability and requiring either microcode update or replacement of the compute node.
